title: Trigonometry: Bearings and Triangle Diagrams Checkpoint
description: Check whether you can build and evaluate bearing diagrams with correct orientation, local north lines, labels, and included angles.

questions.question: Which bearing points directly west?
questions.explanation: A 270° clockwise turn from north points west.

questions.question: A bearing of 135° should be drawn in which general direction?
options: Northeast
Southeast
Southwest
Northwest
questions.explanation: 135° is between 090° and 180°, so the direction is southeast.

questions.question: From station S, point T has bearing 018° and point U has bearing 096°. What included angle should be marked at S?
questions.explanation: Both rays start at S, so subtract the bearings: 096° - 018° = 78°.

questions.question: A route says: From A, travel 8 km on bearing 055° to B. From B, travel 6 km on bearing 150° to C. Which drawing step is correct?
options: Measure both 055° and 150° from the north line at A
Draw a new north line at B before measuring the 150° bearing
Draw BC before drawing AB
Place the 150° label on segment AC
questions.explanation: The second bearing begins at B, so it must be measured from a north line at B.

questions.question: From P, Q is 9 km away on bearing 300°. Which statement describes segment PQ?
options: It points generally northeast from P
It points generally southeast from P
It points generally southwest from P
It points generally northwest from P
questions.explanation: 300° is between 270° and 360°, so PQ points northwest from P.

questions.question: From X to Y, the bearing is 215°. What is the back bearing from Y to X?
questions.correctAnswer: 035° or 35° or 035 degrees or 35 degrees or 035 or 35

questions.question: In triangle ABC, AB and BC are the two traveled legs. Which vertex is the turn point where the included angle between BA and BC may be marked?
options: A
B
C
Any point on AC
questions.explanation: The route turns at B. The angle between BA and BC is inside the triangle at vertex B.

questions.question: Describe how to draw this diagram: From M, N is 4 km away on bearing 020° and O is 7 km away on bearing 110°.
questions.correctAnswer: Draw point M with a north line. From M, draw MN 20° clockwise from north and label it 4 km. From M, draw MO 110° clockwise from north and label it 7 km, then connect N to O.
questions.explanation: Both bearings start at M, so both rays use the same north line at M, and NO completes the triangle.

questions.question: If a diagram shows a bearing angle measured counterclockwise from north, the bearing has been marked incorrectly.
questions.explanation: Standard bearings are measured clockwise from north, so counterclockwise measurement reverses the intended direction.

questions.question: A student draws AB on bearing 040° and BC on bearing 125°, then marks 85° at A as the included angle of triangle ABC. Explain what should be checked or corrected.
questions.correctAnswer: The 85° difference compares bearings only if both bearings start from the same point. In a route A to B to C, the included angle between BA and BC is at B, so the student should use the back bearing from B to A and the bearing from B to C.
questions.explanation: For a two-leg route, the included angle at the turn point uses BA and BC, not the two forward bearings measured from different points.

questions.question: Which checklist best matches a complete bearing triangle diagram?
options: Points labeled, distances labeled, bearings measured clockwise from local north lines, and the direct side drawn when needed
Only the final answer written, with no compass directions
All angles measured from east because east is horizontal
One north line drawn anywhere on the page for every route leg
questions.explanation: A complete diagram needs labeled points and sides, clockwise bearings from the correct local north lines, and the direct side that completes the triangle.
